title: Installation of a Wing Tank Access Panel and Leak Check after Closure

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

abstract: Installation of a wing tank access panel, covering the wet sealed closure and the retained seal closure, the single torque sequence and the pressure and refuel leak checks that release the tank.

sections.purpose: This task installs a wing tank access panel to the closure standard fitted to the aircraft, and does the leak checks that release the tank back to service.
sections.job_setup_note: Confirm the closure standard before you start and use only the torque sequence published for that standard. A wet sealed closure has a cure hold before the tank can be refuelled and the hold cannot be shortened by raising the temperature. On aircraft with the retained face seal, do not apply sealant into the groove; the fillet at the panel edge is for smoothness only and sealant in the groove will hold the seal off its seat.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm that the tank is clean, that the tool count is complete and that no person or equipment remains inside. WARNING: DO NOT CLOSE A TANK BEFORE THE TOOL COUNT IS COMPLETE AND SIGNED. A TOOL LEFT IN A TANK IS A LOOSE ARTICLE IN A FUEL SYSTEM. 2. Clean the seal land or the groove and the panel face. 3. Fit the protective sleeves AGS540148-51 at each fastener position where the standard requires them. CAUTION: ON THE RETAINED SEAL STANDARD DO NOT APPLY SEALANT INTO THE GROOVE. SEALANT IN THE GROOVE HOLDS THE SEAL OFF ITS SEAT AND THE PANEL WILL WEEP. 4. For a wet sealed closure, apply the sealant bead to the pattern in the instructions and within the stated open time. 5. For a retained seal closure, install the seal in the groove and check that it is fully seated over the whole perimeter. 6. Offer the panel up squarely and start every fastener by hand. 7. Torque the fasteners in the single sequence published for the closure standard, in three stages. 8. Install the transmitter D2810138674936 and the switch BE49012-14 through the panel with their own seals. 9. Re-secure the internal harness at the clamp ROD517260-78 and confirm that it does not bear on the seal. 10. Apply the edge fillet for aerodynamic smoothness. 11. For a wet sealed closure, wait for the full cure hold before any pressure is applied. 12. Do the tank pressure leak check at the value in the instructions and hold for the stated period. 13. Refuel the tank and do a visual leak check at the panel edge after two hours and again after twenty-four hours. 14. Check the valve at FIN 44QT for correct operation.
sections.close_out: Remove the ventilation equipment and restore the drain valves. Record the closure standard, the torque sequence used, the pressure decay figure and both refuel leak check results on the maintenance record. Report any weep at the twenty-four hour check before the aircraft is released.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Steps 4 and 11 apply to the wet sealed closure; steps 3 and 5 apply post MOD-159460.

safety_precautions: Do not close a tank before the tool count is complete and signed.
Do not shorten the sealant cure hold by raising the temperature.
Do not apply sealant into the retained seal groove.
